hypotheses.title: Keep expression intermediates unmaterialized until a value escapes the evaluator
hypotheses.description: Replace the recursive evaluator's mandatory owned Value result at every expression node with an internal transient result in spur/spur-core/src/simulator/core/eval.rs: Borrowed(&Value), Int(i64), Bool(bool), or Owned(Value). Keep the existing public eval signature and materialize one canonical Value only when the result escapes to its caller or becomes a stored collection member. Variable loads return a borrow; read-only projections of borrowed lists, tuples, maps, options and variants return a borrow where their lifetime permits it. Arithmetic and boolean subtrees carry native scalar results through their parents without constructing Value, computing its signature, or dropping it at each node. Comparisons use native scalar comparisons only where exactly equivalent; heterogeneous and composite comparisons fall back to the existing Value equality/order semantics. Owned aggregate constructors, mutation, string semantics, iteration order, CFG vertices, environment writes and all execution boundaries remain unchanged. This is one evaluator representation mechanism, not a change to Value's persistent layout or the compiler's CFG. Route unsupported or lifetime-complicated operations through the existing owned behavior. Preserve left-to-right evaluation, short-circuiting, exact RuntimeError values and Rust overflow/division behavior, including invalid expressions. Keep a test-only independent copy of the current evaluator for differential tests under both hashing policies. Add thread-local diagnostic counts exported via util_stats.rs for borrowed operands, scalar intermediates and materializations, with no atomic update per expression node. No config or scheduler change. Treatment: proposed process-wide performance replacement, no run-variant bit or probability contrast. A runtime old/new path is technically possible, but a same-session depth-per-run contrast does not identify the speedup and keeping both engines changes the code layout under test. Admission therefore explicitly requires the judge to accept the perf-specific cross-binary throughput prediction below; do not claim this is an inherently impossible per-run switch or silently translate it into a depth-probability prediction.
hypotheses.rationale: The recorded 2026-09-03 bench profile at c5e49c2 names eval at 7.47% self time, Value::clone at 2.67%, and Value::new at 2.55%. Those historical weights bound a plausible opportunity; they are not current measurements and their entire sum is not removable. Current b86baad eval.rs still recursively creates an owned Value for scalar literals, arithmetic results and boolean results, clones every Var, and clones aggregate parents before read-only projections. The diff from c5e49c2 to b86baad in eval.rs only changes string concatenation and integer formatting. cfg.rs:981-985 keeps an entire pure expression as one nested Expr, so nested arithmetic/guard intermediates are present at runtime rather than already flattened into required stores. The source therefore preserves the named repeated work. Eliminating roughly half the historical evaluator/construction/clone cluster would buy about 6-7% throughput, enough to test against the 5% layout floor, but current scheduler costs or optimized-away scalar construction may erase that margin. The closed value-repr-shrink-hot-variants and unshare-for-try-unwrap attempts optimized each persistent value operation; this proposal removes intermediate operations inside expression evaluation. It does not duplicate merged trace-print-format-pipeline-direct-write or held handler-invocation-fixed-overhead-take-env. No increase in per-run depth probability is predicted.
hypotheses.generalityArgument: The evaluator executes the same language expressions for every protocol without consulting handler names, roles, oracle depth, run outcomes or scheduler policy. All persistent values, signatures, errors, stores, counters, histories and random draws must remain identical for equal input execution. Faster evaluation should multiply the rate of independent opportunities on every protocol in proportion to its expression cost; the panel remains necessary because complex aggregate-heavy programs may gain less or regress.

prediction.mechanism: Perf-specific frozen observable: candidate/baseline runs per explore-second on the unchanged general_vr campaign lies in [1.06,1.12] across paired seeds, above the recorded 5% build-layout floor. The source-verified work reduction is fewer owned intermediate Values and clones per identical expression tree. The epoch primary remains fixed-grid depth>=8 events/sec and must exceed 1.05 of baseline; whole-campaign depth>=8/sec must also exceed 1.05, with the normal panel and regression checks. These are per-second gains only; matched per-run depth probabilities are expected unchanged. Do not divide fixed-grid rates by whole-campaign throughput to manufacture a per-run effect. No treatment bit is proposed; this explicitly needs perf-specific cross-binary admission.
prediction.independentObservable: On an equal-work fixed-seed golden set, the number of canonical Value constructions plus Value clones inside evaluator calls falls by at least 25%, counted in test-only instrumentation around both evaluators; unmaterialized_results counts only a transient result consumed by a parent without conversion, excluding top-level results and owned fallbacks. Preserve exact returned kinds/signatures/errors for generated valid and invalid Expr trees under NoHashing and WithHashing. Fixed single-thread replay/standard cases for VR, Paxos, Raft and language fixtures must match ordered execution/trace/log rows, RNG tapes, step counts, end reasons, environment write counters and every pre-existing utilization counter. Session-global adaptive tables must be held equal for these equal-work comparisons; racing ordinary campaign sessions cannot establish bitwise equivalence. New diagnostic counters alone may differ. All scheduled labels and Env::set calls remain in place.
prediction.falsifier: Close if unmaterialized_results is below 10,000,000 per normal chunk, if the paired throughput interval lies entirely below 1.06 or the final throughput estimate does not clear the 5% layout floor, if equal-work evaluator constructions-plus-clones fall by less than 25%, or if any semantic/RNG/history/pre-existing-counter equality fails. Cost clause: no shared hot-path throughput loss is allowed; the prediction requires >=1.06 overall, every campaign arm must remain >=0.97 throughput, and the full protocol panel must pass. Close rather than merge if fixed-grid or whole-campaign depth>=8/sec fails its 1.05 requirement after the normal chunk cap. A semantic discrepancy is an implementation defect, never evidence of useful schedule search. An uncertain old-profile magnitude does not authorize rewriting this prediction after sampling.
prediction.measurementClarification: Frozen before sampling: process-wide perf replacement, no treatment bit and no per-run depth improvement claim. Treatment is the exported candidate binary; control is the exact paired baseline binary, each with unchanged general_vr.json and ordinary independently reset 300-second chunks. Campaign throughput is sum(runs)/sum(explore seconds) on each side across the same completed paired seeds; report each paired-seed ratio and the aggregate. Fixed four-grid-arm depth>=8/sec and whole-campaign depth>=8/sec are separate populations and must each exceed 1.05. Never infer a grid per-run effect by dividing by whole-campaign throughput. Per-arm throughput must be at least 0.97 on the completed paired evidence. Use existing uncertainty reporting without treating run count as independent replication of binary layout. Normal minimum two chunks and maximum four apply to an effect claim; early termination for semantic, supply or cost failure cannot confirm the multi-chunk prediction.
prediction.acceptanceClarification: The proposed [1.06,1.12] campaign throughput band, >=25% equal-work evaluator constructions-plus-clones reduction, >=10,000,000 unmaterialized_results per normal chunk, exact semantic/recording/pre-existing-counter equality, >1.05 grid and campaign primary rates, per-arm >=0.97 throughput and ordinary full-panel/regression guards all remain frozen. At cap, close if an acceptance gate fails or remains unestablished. A final estimate below 1.06 fails the minimum throughput prediction even if it exceeds the 1.05 layout guard. An estimate above 1.12 is an overshoot of the predicted band, not evidence that the band was met; any decision to retain it must report that distinction. A high firing count or reduced work alone does not establish useful speedup.

equalWorkFrozenProtocol.timing: Correctness and operation counts only; no throughput or speed measurement outside the ordinary grader.
equalWorkFrozenProtocol.config: Use the current scheduler_configs/loop/bench.json scalar config copied only to the isolated test artifact directory, with num_runs_per_config=64, max_iterations=1500 and stats=true. Keep all other bench fields identical: servers3, writes3, reads6, keys1, crashes2, concurrent writes2, dependency_density[0.0]. Use standard exploration, one worker, no campaign; session_seed=1000,1001,1002 in separate fresh sessions. Do not edit the checked-in config.
equalWorkFrozenProtocol.executionModes: For each protocol/seed/hash policy run the reference and candidate evaluator on the same deterministic inputs with fresh identical simulator and adaptive-table state. Also replay the full recorded tapes from those reference executions through each evaluator with identical initial state. Compare completion and the full recorded order; a replay mismatch cannot be dropped from the corpus.
equalWorkFrozenProtocol.operationAccounting: The >=25% reduction denominator is the total canonical Value constructions plus Value clone calls performed during reference evaluator calls on the protocol standard runs above, summed over all three protocols, all three seeds and both hash policies with unit weight per operation. Count every Value construction, including with_sig and composite/escape materialization, and every Value clone recursively initiated during the evaluator call, including collection-member clones in owned fallbacks. Exclude outside-evaluator setup, scheduler, comparison/assertion and reference-output retention. Apply the same dynamic call-scope boundaries and recursion counting to both engines. No speed inference from instrumented operation counts. Report each protocol/seed/hash cell as well as the fixed pooled ratio. Replay and generated-expression counts are reported separately and cannot pad the >=25% gate.
equalWorkFrozenProtocol.expressionCases: For each of deterministic generator seeds1000,1001,1002 generate10000 expression cases to maximum depth6 under both hashing policies, with explicit valid and invalid cases, all Expr variants either generated or covered in an explicit table, and local/node bindings covering scalar and nested collection kinds. Freeze generator and explicit table before its first comparison. Include integer extrema, arithmetic overflow, zero division/remainder, invalid left operand plus failing/panicking right operand, mixed-type comparisons, short-circuit And/Or/Coalesce, missing keys, nil unwrap, negative/out-of-range indexing, and empty nested aggregates. Compare kind/signature or exact RuntimeError or panic outcome. Run semantic tests under debug and release profiles, preserving wrapping versus panic behavior in each.
equalWorkFrozenProtocol.fixtures: Run the existing compiler_integration, map_iteration_identity and replay_prefix_fidelity suites with their checked-in fixture inputs/configurations. Add evaluator differential unit coverage for the existing timer,relay,kv,mapiter,fanout,ghost fixture programs where their suite runs exercise the evaluator. Fixture coverage supplements but never changes the protocol operation-count denominator.
equalWorkFrozenProtocol.identityChecks: For the protocol standard and replay corpus compare ordered execution/trace/log rows, RNG tapes, step counts, end reasons, environment values/signatures/write counts and every pre-existing utilStats counter. Normalize only container metadata/order using semantic row keys, never event fields. New eval_transient diagnostics alone may differ.

review.redTeam: The historical profile is bench.json at c5e49c2, not the current adaptive general campaign at b86baad. eval self time includes irreducible expression dispatch and aggregate/string work, while Value::clone and Value::new include callers outside eval; adding their weights does not identify removable time. Borrowed/Owned/Int/Bool dispatch, materialization boundaries, lifetime fallbacks and thread-local counters can replace the avoided overhead. Large transient enum returns may still copy many bytes. A 25% operation-count reduction can remove cheap calls while leaving costly ones, so it need not buy 6% wall time. The upper 12% prediction is particularly optimistic against the historical 12.69% whole cluster. Independent builds have shown 4-5% throughput variation, just below the 6% lower prediction, and additional paired seeds do not remove a fixed layout effect. Faster wall-budget sessions change adaptive feedback populations even with exact single-run semantics. Most seriously, rewritten invalid-expression evaluation order, error precedence, overflow behavior, heterogeneous comparisons, map key signatures, or borrowed projections can silently alter the protocol histories whose violations we count.
review.argumentScoreReason: 7, the low end of the verified mechanism-to-observable range: current source establishes a concrete repeated operation, a safe representation boundary, surviving nested Expr trees, and an independent equal-work work-count falsifier; the profile and prior closures are correctly dated and independently verified. This grade is not a forecast that the 6-12% effect will occur. Historical profile scope and no current per-site frequencies prevent an 8 or 9.
review.costReason: 2. Although exec.rs/history.rs need not change, this replaces expression semantics used by all protocol execution and can invalidate correctness and measurement validity. This is the rubric correctness cost, not a charge for implementation size or time.
verifiedEvidence: Main spur HEAD is b86baad. research/observations/PROFILE.md records 2026-09-03 bench.json, 30 threads, c5e49c2, eval<NoHashing> 7.47%, Value::clone 2.67%, Value::new 2.55% self time. The proposal correctly describes these as historical, not current.

Find/ListAccess/TupleAccess/Unwrap/Coalesce clone projection results after recursively materializing parents. These are current source mechanisms, not evidence of their runtime frequency.

Native same-kind integer/Boolean equality and ordering match Value implementations; heterogeneous/composite cases require existing fallback. Arithmetic division and overflow behavior cannot be replaced with a different checked-error contract.

util_stats.rs already has process enable/reset and thread-local run state with finish-run folding. Existing baseline cache 34b5ef40e3bf-30-f9daa01b-300-g870d4c11-s3d907a50.json has 1169 counter names on its first chunk and no eval_transient keys. Proposed counters and their 10M floor are new predictions, not existing observations.

Root subsequently reported its completed close at d06096e: assigned applicability31.28%<60%, tape4.77x>1.5, throughput0.8723<0.95, grid depth8/sec0.9012, campaign0.8555, AOS per-run0.7328, rawprefix/plan1.130, adjusted1.0628[0.9408,1.2006], zero violations in532260 runs. implementationConstraints: Restrict subject edits to evaluator internals, util_stats support and meaningful acceptance/export tests. Preserve public eval/load/store behavior; do not change CFG vertices, Env::set calls, Value persistent representation, scheduler, campaign, cap, RNG streams, protected subjects or harness.

Keep the reference evaluator test-only and independent. Its recursive calls must invoke the reference, not the candidate wrapper. Under both hashing policies compare kind, signature, errors and panic/overflow behavior in the same build mode; include invalid left operands with erroring/panicking right operands to test error precedence, short-circuit And/Or/Coalesce, empty/missing projections, negative indices, integer extrema, zero divisors and composite/heterogeneous comparisons.

Only return borrows tied to the immutable environment or another demonstrably live owner. Never borrow out of a temporary Owned result across its destruction. Materialize canonical Values for map keys and every storage/public escape; use existing fallback when ownership/lifetime or semantics are complicated. Avoid unsafe lifetime extension.

Count constructions and clones identically in reference and candidate test-only instrumentation, including fallback/materialization operations during evaluator calls. Define the common denominator as total reference constructions plus clones over the fixed equal-work corpus. Commit the corpus and counting boundaries before collecting the comparative result; do not select only scalar-heavy examples after seeing savings.

unmaterialized_results counts only Borrowed/Int/Bool transient results actually consumed by a parent without canonical conversion, not all evaluator invocations, top-level results or owned fallbacks. Aggregate thread-local counts with explicit session reset and final flush so short/failing runs and the last worker run are counted once; verify aggregate export and no bleed across sessions. No shared atomic update per expression node.

Exact fixed-work acceptance uses deterministic single-thread standard/replay runs of VR, Paxos, Raft and language fixtures with identical adaptive starting tables/updates. Compare semantic ordered rows, seeds, tapes, steps, end reasons, environments and all pre-existing utilization counters. Do not use raw container-file byte equality with nondeterministic metadata, or racing wall-clock campaigns, as the definition of semantic equality.
A mismatch is an implementation defect to repair before grading, never a protocol finding. Equal-work parity and work savings do not authorize weakening the frozen campaign utility or panel gates.

Value equality/order is kind-specific with deterministic cross-type ordering, not signature-first. Preserve actual current Value::cmp semantics and separately preserve returned signatures. Do not hoist right-operand evaluation past the current left-side type check, or introduce an early type check where the current branch first evaluates both operands.

hypotheses.title: Keep causal-chain scheduling priorities through replay suffixes and demote chains at sampled change points
hypotheses.description: Use the existing prefix-replay treatment population to test a PCT-style causal-chain scheduler after the existing signal-cut tape is exhausted. Parent admission, tape cut, capacity, eight-child limit and plan-only control remain exactly as in the baseline. Add run-local chain identifiers for executable records and ChannelSend continuations. Before activation maintain identity propagation but leave effective priorities unchanged. A client request, timer firing, initialization/recovery root or otherwise parentless event starts a chain; RPC calls, asynchronous sends, spawned receiver records and their continuations inherit their creator's chain. A channel wakeup preserves the waiting reader's chain; it does not merge unrelated chains. Pending pre-cut records whose ancestry was not tracked receive separate root identifiers at activation. After tape exhaustion, activate only once the child's own existing ghost-with-pending-crash signal has fired. Draw two distinct future change points uniformly without replacement over the remaining frozen cap; if fewer than three steps remain, stay inert. Use a private deterministic hash stream seeded from the child schedule seed, with no reads from simulator RNG streams. Give chains a deterministic random total order keyed by that seed and chain id. At each change point demote the chain of the last executed executable record below all chains not yet demoted; retain this relative order for the rest of the suffix. A second demotion of the same chain is counted and changes no other order. Do not globally pick events by this order: run the stock queue-class draw, including timer-context bias and its empty-queue fallbacks. In the existing within-queue selector, use the chain key as a lexicographic ranking above the original score only among the exact candidates that the tournament already sampled; equal-chain candidates use the original score and index tie behavior. For the non-tournament selector, use the ordinary selected event unchanged and count that exclusion, so the mechanism does not silently redefine proportional selection. Preserve ordinary priority draws at creation even when chain keys govern ranking. Existing reservations, FIFO, crash holds, fresh-first, pair-order and client request release still run, and instrumentation compares the final legal pick with the stock sampled pick without drawing more randomness. Non-executable faults and timers keep their original scoring; their created executable descendants acquire or inherit chains. Add chain propagation in core/state.rs, core/exec.rs, core/scheduler.rs and path.rs, activation information in explorer.rs/rng.rs, and utilization exports/tests. Do not alter hashes, trace ids, causal_operation_id, protocol state or logging. No config field, nested dose, new treatment bit, state checkpoint or shared learner.
hypotheses.rationale: The unattempted causal-chain idea has a verified missing object: records retain priority through local continuations, but newly sent records draw independently at every hop. PCT demotions need a persistent chain to move as a unit. The existing tournament offers real authority once candidates are sampled; comparing chain order directly over that same candidate set avoids assuming that multiplying a narrow score band can change eligibility or queue choice. Restricting the policy to supplied early replay suffixes places coherent execution and subsequent interleaving changes near an observed fault race while preserving the original path to it. This is not a hold on an origin or recovery class and does not claim that long queue-free stretches were absent before. Two change points are the structural depth-three PCT search choice, not an empirical dose sweep. PCT probability bounds for fixed threads do not transfer to dynamically spawned chains; the claim here is empirical search utility. Ordinary signal-cut parents and existing same-step return counts suggest applicability, but the new child activation, sampled multi-chain contests and surviving suffix must be measured.
hypotheses.generalityArgument: The persistent unit is causality in the simulator's execution graph, independent of message names, contents, protocol roles or oracle labels. Any protocol with asynchronous sends can exhibit chains whose relative interleaving matters. Queue selection, timer admission, legal event sets and fault semantics remain the same. The protocol panel must verify both clean behavior and known-bug discovery; throughput or selective VR depth alone cannot establish general value.

treatmentBit.name: replayPrefix
treatmentBit.share: The existing salted half of replay slots, approximately one quarter of non-probe grid runs; unchanged assignment and empty-slot behavior.
treatmentBit.control: The existing replay-slot runs without replayPrefix, which reuse a parent's configuration and workload and run a fresh schedule. Non-slot runs and AOS receive no new policy.
treatmentBit.identity: The bit continues to mean schedule-prefix replay from a corpus parent. No new bit, nested run-id dose, campaign arm, or protected registration edit. This is a replacement of the prefix-replay search mechanism, not a reinterpretation of a selector or fault bit.
treatmentBit.contrast: Intention to treat on all prefix-tagged slots, including unfilled and failed branch attempts, probe-free and matched on existing co-bits. Also compute the candidate prefix/plan-only ratio divided by the paired baseline prefix/plan-only ratio. A filled-only ratio is descriptive, never the treatment estimate.
treatmentBit.inverse: No additional inverse cell: alternatives and initial chain orders are sampled symmetrically, and neither search procedure has a single protocol-independent signed inverse. They are stochastic policies inside the one existing prefix-replay mechanism, not hidden run-id treatment doses.

prediction.mechanism: The probe-free, co-bit-matched prefix/plan-only per-run ratio will be1.20-1.60; its ratio to the paired baseline contrast will be1.15-1.50. Fixed four-grid-arm primary events/sec>=1.06 baseline, whole-campaign events/sec>=1.03 baseline, and AOS depth8 per run>=0.95 baseline. These are separate predictions, not estimates inferred by dividing grid utility by whole-campaign throughput.
prediction.independentObservable: Per300-second chunk, >=40000 prefix children activate before their own cap, >=25000 active children execute >=8 subsequent steps, and >=15000 active children reach at least one change point. At least20% of eligible suffix tournament decisions have >=2 distinct chains in the candidates actually sampled. On those multi-chain sampled contests the final legal winner differs from the shadow stock winner at least15% of the time; fresh-first/pair-order overwrites and same-chain ties are separate counts. Among active children with at least eight suffix dispatches, median consecutive executable dispatches sharing one chain rises at least25% over plan-only children measured after their own first signal, while realized timer dispatch share stays within10% relative of that control. The latter comparison is descriptive and reports readiness/arm strata; the randomized all-slot contrast decides utility. Emit activation delay from tape exhaustion, frozen remaining-cap bins, excluded selector type, change points reached, distinct chains sampled, inherited cross-node sends, same-chain ties, shadow-choice changes before and after merged preferences, and per-arm chain-run-length histograms. Existing counters cannot currently report these quantities; all are added with the mechanism.
prediction.falsifier: Refuted if the matched treatment contrast interval lies wholly below1.20 or its paired baseline-adjusted contrast lies wholly below1.15. Supply below40000 active runs, below15000 reached change points, multi-chain contest share below20%, final dispatch authority below15%, or chain persistence growth below25% refutes the claimed mechanism. A timer-share change above10% requires closing this specification because preserving timer admission in code did not preserve the claimed exposure. Primary<=baseline with more coherent chains is not success. Repeated AOS ratio below0.95 or whole-campaign utility loss prevents merge despite a grid gain. Report replay-family sensitivity rather than treating sibling runs as independent evidence.
prediction.costClause: Cross-binary whole-campaign throughput>=0.97 of paired baseline. The original cap, completed-plan termination and number of histories are unchanged. Do not skip baseline priority samples to claim a speedup: byte-consumption parity is part of the mechanism. All trace and client-history semantics remain ordinary. If supply or dispatch authority fails in the first normal chunk, close before additional chunks/panel. Additional ancestry storage is at most one u64 chain id per executable or buffered executable object, with measured Rust layout growth at most16 bytes per affected Record/ChannelSend/partition-buffered message representation. Run-local chain control and observation storage is at most1024 bytes, excluding existing state and the one chain id per object; use fixed-size counters/histograms. Retain at most two demoted chain ids and derive other chain priorities directly from seed/id, with no dynamically growing per-chain map, ancestry graph or per-step log. Export the relevant size_of layout measurements, maximum run-local allocated bytes, maximum retained demotion entries and count of root allocations; verify fixed bounds against the ordinary trial. Peak process RSS may be reported descriptively but has no paired ratio gate.
prediction.measurementClarification: The20% multi-chain sampled contest share uses all eligible suffix tournament decisions. The15% final choice-change fraction is restricted to multi-chain samples with an executable stock winner, as frozen by the mixed-fault rule; report both denominators and exclusions. New chain metadata and all control histograms must be explicitly implemented. This is a prefix-replay-plus-causal-chain replacement policy contrast versus plan-only, not a randomized estimate of chain ranking alone. Raw1.20-1.60 and paired baseline-adjusted1.15-1.50 remain separate bands; use the existing grader without registration or protocol changes.
prediction.memoryMeasurementClarification: Pre-admission memory correction: the current same-identity baseline cache contains no RSS/resident/peak-memory fields and no matching baseline peak is available in retained observations. A valid paired peak would require additional baseline acquisition, not reinterpretation of a cached metric. No new baseline run, calibration-only round, identity change or cache mutation is authorized by this proposal. The unsupported peak-RSS ratio is therefore removed before admission and replaced by directly checkable bounds on additional mechanism-owned storage. These bounds constrain bookkeeping/corpus growth; they are NOT a claim that total process RSS is unchanged or below the original1.25x/1.15x thresholds. Actual process peak, if collected during the ordinary candidate chunk, is descriptive only.

hypotheses.sourceVerification: Source verified: campaign.rs GridArm admits fresh parents at state.replay_cut, serves CAPACITY=64 and CHILDREN_PER_PARENT=8 round-robin, and distinguishes prefix children from plan-only children. No children are admitted. rng.rs Recording is an Arc<[u64]> and RecRng exposes recording position; replay currently has no public consumed-tape-length/finished-prefix query. core/scheduler.rs computes eligibility with reservations, FIFO, crash holds, and down-victim guards before queue/within-queue choice. Existing replay fidelity is only equality of the child's first signal step with seed.cut_step, not state equality. Baseline seed1000 records 72959 parents,108506 filled prefix children,107830 plan-only children,18454 unfilled slots and56198 same-step signal returns. These are ordinary 300-second supply observations, not proof that the proposed narrower action predicate will fire. Existing source draws new priorities at sends and roots; continuation resumption retains a Record priority. No protected files need editing. Additional verified details: WithinQueueSelector defaults to Tournament{k:10}; select_within_queue samples eligible candidates using Stream::WithinQueue. Queue-class selection separately applies timer_context before within-queue selection. Record has send_ordinal, origin_incarnation, entry_pc and causal_operation_id but no generic chain id. ChannelSend currently has no causal-operation or chain field, so cross-channel propagation must be designed explicitly rather than inferred from client-operation ids.
hypotheses.notes: Blind judge gain5-cost2=3, retained as a substantive but less evidenced scheduling alternative. Frozen clarifications resolve mixed executable/fault ordering, timer-root ancestry, partition propagation and authority denominators before any implementation or experiment. No claim of sound DPOR or transferred PCT guarantee. Before admission, unavailable paired-RSS gates were replaced with bounded additional owned-storage checks; this does not establish total process memory non-regression.

review.redTeam: PCT fixed-thread guarantees do not apply here: chains spawn dynamically, queues are selected separately, only sampled candidates can compete, and merged preferences can overwrite chain order. Most contests may be singleton/same-chain, or the stock winner may be a fault, leaving little authority. A chain can also fan out widely and dominate scheduling until a late cap-relative demotion, suppressing the very mixed-origin order sought. Two cap-uniform change points often occur after plan completion. Preserving timer admission code does not preserve realized timer exposure. Cross-channel ancestry can be lost in buffering/recovery, or parentless roots can collapse into one chain. Carrying metadata on every record may cost more than sparse prefix-child authority can repay.
verifiedEvidence: Main Spur is b86baad3f94ce14dbdf20688b61fd92317a75cc2. Conditional67 is CLOSED after repeated AOS harm; interaction-parent68 is ACTIVE and ungraded for this review. Neither prototype is the baseline.

campaign.rs:424-523 records fresh grid runs, truncates admitted parents at replay_cut.tape_pos, serves prefix children with ReplayRng and plan-only with LiveRng, and compares only signal steps for prefix_faithful. replay_corpus.rs specifies capacity64, eight total children per parent, salted slot/prefix assignment excluding run-cap and timer probes, round-robin service and no child admission.

Baseline cache seed1000 verifies72959 parents,108506 prefix children,107830 plan-only children,18454 unfilled slots,56198 same-step signal returns; seed1001 has71910,108175,107615,17996,54542. These establish early replay supply only, not branch legality, state fidelity, suffix depth, or chain activation.

rng.rs ReplayRng.position returns total output words, not consumed source words; source pos stops growing at source exhaustion, while out continues. A replay-exhaustion query is new. RecRng.next_u32 consumes one recorded u64 and fill_bytes consumes ceil(bytes/8) words. Positions must be recorded-word positions, not high-level draw counts or scheduling steps. Stream isolation still records one interleaved raw tape; changing arms, learned snapshots, caps or readiness can break replay fidelity.

core/scheduler.rs applies crash hold/defer masks, reservations, FIFO and down-victim guards before queue selection; strict timers add an eligibility condition. Queue selection applies timer_context separately. Tournament samples with replacement up to min(k,eligible.len()), default k10; singleton decisions take no within-queue draws. Network selections then pass fresh_first_dispatch and pair_order_dispatch.

fresh_first_dispatch mutates displacement bookkeeping and records counters; pair_order_dispatch also emits counters. Calling either as a shadow/eligibility preview would double count or mutate real state unless selection is factored into a pure preview and a single real commit.

run-specific arms, learner/probe assignment, credit guard, caps, workload/history and feedback merge remain stock. Replay children do not earn extra learner reward by inheriting a parent. hypotheses.title: Resample successful joint arm sets and mutate their uncertain axes
hypotheses.description: Replace independent arm-axis sampling on learner draws with a bounded population search in simulator/arm_selector.rs. Each existing learner/configuration cell retains a ring of its last WARMUP_OBSERVATIONS successful full ArmSet vectors, with their credited-observation indices. Admit vectors only from runs that the learner already observes under its existing coin-or-own-run exposure rule and that earn its unchanged Boolean reward. Retain at most 24 entries and expire entries older than ceil(1/(1-DISCOUNT))=500 credited observations. Repeated vectors from independent successful runs remain repeated population members; no execution tape, plan, workload or state is copied. When at least eight live successes spanning at least two distinct vectors are present, a learner draw samples one population member uniformly and mutates exactly one axis. Choose the mutation axis proportionally to the categorical entropy of that axis's current normalized posterior-leading probabilities, and draw a different direction from the existing coin shares renormalized over the alternatives. If all entropies vanish, choose the axis uniformly. Thus four coordinates preserve a successful joint setting while uncertain coordinates receive exploration. Cells below support retain the current independent marginal sampler. Keep the current adaptive coin share, marginal posteriors, three learner assignments and rewards, per-configuration pooling, cap and all scheduler mechanisms unchanged. Population admission and aging share the current credit write guard. A cell's ordinary coin runs remain fresh exploration, and replay behavior and ordinary reward credit semantics remain unchanged. At draw time aggregate this parent-and-mutation mixture into the exact categorical distribution over the 72 ArmSet values, then sample that distribution. For an observation-only comparison, use the same uniform variate and fixed ArmSet index order to sample the product of the current marginal axis distributions; identical distributions therefore produce no departure. Count the Hamming distance between the actual tuple and this comparison tuple. Record mutation-axis mass from the exact mixture, and add counters and bounded per-cell exports for live support, unique vectors, supported draws, joint total-variation distance and subsequent reward counts on population-sampled runs. Cache the population mixture after each credited update that changes the population, refreshing the entropy weights after every WARMUP_OBSERVATIONS credits. Comparison calculations consume no schedule random numbers. No config field, campaign arm or harness change.
hypotheses.rationale: The existing joint Thompson proposal was weak because 72 combinations divide a discounted window into too few observations to estimate all combination reward rates. Successful-vector resampling uses observed successful tuples directly and needs no estimate for every combination. It also avoids recombining five separately favorable directions into a tuple that was never successful together, a structural limitation left largely unchanged when conditional draws seldom depart from marginal choices. Broad existing reward supply makes the population support falsifiable at the normal horizon. The main risks are reinforcement of frequently sampled tuples, loss of useful multi-axis jumps, and reward/depth misalignment. Independent coin draws and entropy-directed mutation provide escape paths, but they do not prove these risks harmless.
hypotheses.generalityArgument: Population members are complete settings of general scheduling mechanisms, and their fitness is one of the existing protocol-independent rewards. The same success-and-mutation rule works for any protocol's action effects without inspecting handler names, roles, message payloads, oracle traces or known violations. Configurations and workloads are still chosen by the existing campaign; only the mechanism settings of a new execution are adapted.

prediction.mechanism: Treatment: the session-global arm population and learner search distribution, with no new treatment bit. No existing bit is redefined to denote a new population policy. Because both successful-vector supply and marginal posteriors depend on previous population-generated runs, an off draw sharing those tables is not an untreated experiment. Grade this single-model replacement on the cross-binary rung with fresh reset sessions, unchanged campaign arms and the epoch's matched primary population. Frozen paired candidate/baseline depth>=8 per-run ratio is [1.07,1.18]. Require primary events per explore-second >=1.04 and paired throughput >=0.97. This is not a revived 72-cell Thompson estimator or an increased checkpoint offspring budget.
prediction.independentObservable: Per normal 300-second chunk require >=20 learner/configuration cells to make >=100 population draws after satisfying the eight-live-success/two-distinct-vector gate, and >=100000 supported population draws in total. At least 20 percent of these actual selected ArmSets must differ in two or more coordinates from the product-marginal categorical comparison using the same uniform variate and ArmSet index order. Joint total-variation distance from the product-marginal distribution must be >=0.10 on at least half of supported draws; unlike an independent random shadow, this test is zero when the distributions agree. At least two distinct axes must each receive >=10 percent of mutation probability mass across supported draws, and at least 80 percent of population draws must come from cells whose live population contains >=4 distinct successful vectors; report repeated-vector concentration explicitly. Across four chunks, at least two of the three existing per-learner own-run reward rates must be >=1.10 of their corresponding baseline rates, with the third >=0.95. Those baseline rates are already exported; new supported-draw outcome counters additionally report whether sampled vectors succeed when executed again. The fitted population success rate and inherited parent success never count as the new run's outcome. Judge clarification: all live support, unique-vector counts and probability comparisons are read at decision time before this run is observed. Expiration uses the same cell credited-observation clock, not wall time, axis visits or only positive updates. A stored success is live when current_observation_index - success_observation_index <=500; expire greater ages, retain at most the24 most recent remaining successes. Population-supported draws satisfy >=8 live entries and >=2 distinct tuples. Count supported draws separately from changed_joint_draws, which counts tuples different from the product-marginal comparator. The two-coordinate comparison is coupling/order dependent and descriptive; the exact TV gate is the distributional check. Define ArmSet order lexicographically by axis direction indices [crash,retarget,fresh_first,pair_order,request], last axis varying fastest. Mutation-mass fractions are sums of the exact mixture axis masses over supported draws, with supported draws as denominator.
prediction.falsifier: Refute if the primary contrast interval lies entirely below 1.07, the two-coordinate departure share falls below 20 percent, the joint-distribution TV gate fails, or the actual subsequent reward-rate clause fails. Missing the normal-horizon support or firing floors closes the candidate; do not lower the eight-success gate, extend the 500-observation window or pool configurations after observing inadequate supply. Mutation concentrated below the two-axis floor or population diversity below the four-vector clause refutes the claimed exploration mechanism. Throughput below 0.97, primary events-per-second below 1.04 or a panel regression closes on cost or generality. A better broad reward with flat or worse oracle depth refutes transfer, rather than establishing progress. Judge clarification: report repeated material AOS harm as a generality failure even if the selective grid primary rises. A tuple inherited from a successful population member does not inherit its success or any execution evidence.
prediction.measurementClarification: Primary means the same four grid arms in candidate and baseline. The per-run band and per-second guard use that population; overall throughput is separately reported. Also report AOS and whole-campaign per-run/per-second outcomes, with unchanged panel/regression guards. A selective grid gain with repeated material AOS or panel harm does not establish general search improvement. No seed selection or retrospective baseline substitution.
prediction.horizonClarification: Normal chunks are independently reset 300-second sessions, up to the existing four-chunk cap. Per-chunk applicability/firing gates apply at that horizon. Own-run reward clauses apply to pooled completed paired seeds at the final decision, with four chunks required to claim confirmation of the specified four-chunk reward prediction. Early close is allowed for predeclared applicability, cost or harm gates; do not claim a four-chunk result from an early stop.

hypotheses.notes: Judge reviewed blind. Rubric cost corrected from 2 to 0 because these changes do not alter execution, history, event accounting or linearizability recording. Evidence for the proposed gain is thin; score is an argument grade, not a numerical effect forecast.

review.redTeam: A ring of successful tuples samples policy frequency times reward probability, not reward probability alone. Repeated popular successes can crowd out rare settings and reinforce whichever learner policy already dominates. Entropy-directed mutation may repeatedly break the one useful axis; preserving four settings can inhibit necessary multi-axis jumps. At low reward rates the500-credit age window can fail the eight-success gate, particularly in colder cells. A shared-uniform lexicographic comparison can have large Hamming distance for reasons of tuple ordering; that is not proof of useful diversity. Existing broad rewards have already improved while target depth and AOS declined. Exact72-tuple distribution maintenance adds hot-path work.

Endogenous learner/coin tags and shared random comparison choices are diagnostic, not randomized treatment controls.

The current selector leading_probability computes pairwise-normal leading weights, then sample_axis_leading multiplies by ArmSet coin probabilities. Pure normalized leading weights for mutation entropy and final coin-weighted probabilities for product-marginal comparison are different quantities and must remain explicit.

DISCOUNT=0.998 and warmup24 are current. ceil(1/(1-DISCOUNT)) mathematically yields500; this proposed success-age window is a new cell-clock expiry rule, not identical to existing per-direction discounting.

The pool full72-combination Thompson alternative is kept but not buildable as written because its0.995 discount and per-combination leader requirement undersupply evidence. Successful-tuple resampling avoids fitting72 independent reward rates, but does not by itself solve adaptive selection bias.

The eight-live-success and diversity gates are not implied by aggregate baseline positives. A/B/C own-run rates are approximately5.83%,17.83%,5.42%; cells differ and coin rewards are lower. Population support remains a prediction to test at the normal horizon.

It is not exactly the already-kept Thompson mechanism because it has no72-cell posterior, but there is no new interaction evidence. requiredImplementationConstraints: Check and remove expired successes on every credited cell update, including unsuccessful runs. Adding a positive, evicting the oldest entry, expiry, or a24-credit entropy refresh invalidates the mixture cache. A draw reads one consistent live population/cache snapshot.

Define entropy from normalized posterior-leading weights, before coin weighting, as proposed. Alternative directions use the existing coin shares renormalized excluding the parent direction. Components change exactly one axis; aggregate exact mixture probabilities across repeated entries and coincident child tuples.

Sample the resulting72-tuple distribution directly with one selector random variate. The product-marginal comparator uses that same variate and fixed lexicographic order, consumes no additional schedule draws and is observation-only. When population support fails, retain the baseline independent sampler and count fallback.

No latent parent or executed mutation axis is uniquely determined by a tuple drawn from the aggregated mixture. Export expected mutation-axis probability mass; do not invent a realized parent lineage or offspring reward that the algorithm did not sample.

Update outcome counters from this run actual completed Boolean reward. Stored successes and replayed histories are not fresh confirmations of the sampled tuple. Existing credit rules remain unchanged; no cross-learner or extra replay credit.

Bound population entries at24 per learner/cell; report maximum repeated-vector share and unique-live counts. Do not deduplicate repeated successes, extend expiry, lower support, or change one-axis mutation after observing supply.

perfAdmission.decision: admit with an explicit written exception to the default per-run-switch rule
perfAdmission.reason: The skill default permits no bit only when the mechanism cannot switch per run. That literal default is not satisfied here. The same skill explicitly says nothing besides its protected paths/hard stops is a veto and written judgment governs. I approve an exception because the causal claim is less CPU work for identical executions; depth probability within one process is expected unchanged and cannot measure the proposed per-second gain. A runtime old/new evaluator and direct timings are technically possible, but keeping both adds branch/code-layout costs and would measure a different combined implementation. Cross-binary speed with independent semantic and operation-count tests is a scientifically admissible performance question already tied to the goal rate and the earlier formatting experiment. This does not establish clean randomized identification of the precise gain: persistent layout effects and wall-budget adaptive differences remain confounders, are reported explicitly, and ordinary panel/utility guards remain binding. No harness or skill change is authorized or required.
perfAdmission.boundary: This is admission to an experiment, not approval of a result or permission to claim per-run exploration improvement. The 6% lower edge is above the recorded 5% caveat but not safely far from it. Do not treat repeated seeds as independent binary-layout replications, replace the observable with depth probability, or claim that per-run switching is impossible.

Chain demotion remains5-2=3, population mutation3-0=3. Root completion update closes frontier69 without boosting the evaluator score or changing its effect prediction.
